newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello eyes 15 pct or more Australian GST - paper.
newsitem.headline: Costello eyes 15 pct or more Australian GST - paper.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello has told government politicians that a goods and services tax (GST) of at least 15 percent was needed to abolish existing sales taxes and fund necessary income tax cuts, The Australian newspaper said on Wednesday.

"Coalition backbenchers said the cost of abolishing sales tax would be a GST rate equivalent to around six percent, with another three to four percent for removing petrol excise and an additional three percent to remove state payroll taxes," the paper said.
"Income tax cuts of more than A$5 billion would need a GST rate of at least two percent.".
The combined amount proposed by Costello would be at least 15 percent.

Costello also told politicians that unless tax reform was done urgently, the government would face a political problem with people earning average weekly earnings being hit by the top marginal tax rate for the first time, The Australian said.
Costello held a meeting with the politicians on Monday evening to outline the government's agenda for tax reform.
He told reporters after the meeting that the politicians genuinely wanted tax reform.
The government is widely expected to propose some form of consumption tax or GST in the next election campaign scheduled for the first half of 1999.
The coalition -- which lost what was regarded as an easy-win election in 1993 with a GST policy -- pledged in the 1996 election not to introduce a consumption tax in its first three-year term.
But a series of recent opinion polls have showed growing community support for a GST and Prime Minister John Howard has not ruled out its introduction in the second term of government.
